objectives: Explain central + peripheral tolerance + the genetic basis of monogenic autoimmunity.
Survey major autoimmune diseases + their immunopathology.
Classify hypersensitivity reactions + understand allergy + Th2 biology.

slides.title: Tolerance + autoimmunity: central vs peripheral, AIRE + Treg + IPEX
slides.body:
**Self-tolerance** — the absence of immune responses against self-antigens — is enforced at multiple levels.

**Central tolerance** — during lymphocyte development in primary lymphoid organs.
- **Thymus (T cells)**: **negative selection** in medulla — thymocytes with TCRs binding self-peptide–MHC complexes with high affinity undergo apoptosis (Bcl-2/Bim-mediated). Some intermediate-affinity self-reactive thymocytes are diverted into the **Treg lineage** (Foxp3⁺).
- **AIRE (autoimmune regulator)** — transcription factor in medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs) that drives ectopic expression of >3000 tissue-specific antigens (insulin, thyroglobulin, retinal antigens, salivary proteins, others). Without AIRE, tissue-specific antigens are not encountered in the thymus → self-reactive T cells escape → multi-organ autoimmunity.
- **APECED** (Autoimmune Polyendocrinopathy-Candidiasis-Ectodermal Dystrophy) = **APS-1**: autosomal-recessive AIRE mutations → mucocutaneous candidiasis + adrenal insufficiency + hypoparathyroidism + multiple endocrinopathies + anti-IFN-α/ω antibodies (which paradoxically increase risk of severe COVID-19 — Casanova et al.).
- **Bone marrow (B cells)**: immature B cells with strong self-reactivity undergo receptor editing (light-chain re-rearrangement) or, failing that, deletion. Anergy in the periphery silences additional self-reactive clones.

**Peripheral tolerance** — backup mechanisms outside primary lymphoid organs.
- **Anergy**: T or B cells that encounter antigen without costimulation (signal 2) become functionally unresponsive.
- **Deletion**: activation-induced cell death (AICD) via Fas-FasL.
- **Ignorance**: anatomic + cellular sequestration (immune-privileged sites: eye, testis, CNS, fetus).
- **Regulatory T cells (Tregs)**: FOXP3⁺ CD4⁺CD25⁺ T cells; suppress effector responses via CTLA-4 (sequester CD80/86), IL-10, TGFβ, granzyme, IL-2 sequestration. Critical peripheral checkpoint.
- **IPEX** (Immune dysregulation Polyendocrinopathy Enteropathy X-linked): X-linked **FOXP3** mutations → no functional Tregs → fatal multi-organ autoimmunity in male infants (enteropathy, T1D, eczema, thyroiditis, cytopenias). Now treated by hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation; gene-corrected autologous HSC therapy in development.
- **Checkpoint receptors**: **CTLA-4** (binds CD80/86 with higher affinity than CD28; constitutively on Tregs, induced on activated T cells); **PD-1** (induced on chronic activation; binds PD-L1/L2; exhaustion + tolerance). Both targets of cancer immunotherapy (Allison + Honjo Nobel 2018) — a 'lifting the brakes' approach.

**Genetic + environmental contributions to autoimmunity**:
- **Genetic**: HLA alleles dominate (HLA-B*27 + ankylosing spondylitis OR ~80; HLA-DR3 + DR4 + T1D; HLA-DRB1*15:01 + MS; HLA-DQ2/DQ8 + celiac; HLA-DRB1*04:01-*04:04 *shared epitope* + RA). Also: PTPN22 (multi-disease), STAT4, IL-23R, IRF5, CD40, FCGR, etc. Large-scale GWAS implicate hundreds of loci.
- **Environmental**: infections (molecular mimicry — group A strep + rheumatic fever; EBV + MS, multiple sclerosis), microbiome perturbations, smoking (RA), low vitamin D, hygiene, gluten + celiac, drugs (procainamide + drug-induced lupus, hydralazine, anti-TNF paradoxical autoimmunity).
- **Sex bias**: most autoimmune diseases are female-predominant (SLE 9:1, Sjögren 9:1, Hashimoto 7:1, MS 3:1, RA 3:1) — sex hormones + X-inactivation skewing + XIST-RNA neoantigens may contribute (Anguera, Chang labs).

slides.title: Major autoimmune diseases: RA, SLE, MS, T1D, psoriasis, IBD, Hashimoto's
slides.body:
**Rheumatoid arthritis (RA)** — chronic symmetric polyarticular inflammation; ~1% prevalence.
- **Autoantibodies**: rheumatoid factor (anti-IgG-Fc, classic) + **anti-CCP/anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPA)** (Schellekens 1998+; high specificity; predict erosive disease).
- **Pathogenesis**: PAD enzymes citrullinate proteins (in lung + gum; smoking + *Porphyromonas gingivalis* implicated) → ACPA → immune complexes + complement → synovitis. Th17 + TNF + IL-6 dominate.
- **Therapy**: methotrexate (anchor); biologics — **TNF blockers** (infliximab, adalimumab, etanercept); IL-6 (tocilizumab, sarilumab); CTLA-4-Ig (abatacept); anti-CD20 (rituximab); **JAK inhibitors** (tofacitinib, baricitinib, upadacitinib). Transformed the field.

**Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)** — multi-system autoimmune disease; ~9:1 female:male.
- **Autoantibodies**: **ANA** (anti-nuclear antibodies; ~95% sensitivity); **anti-dsDNA** (specific; correlates with nephritis); **anti-Sm** (specific); anti-Ro/SSA (neonatal lupus, Sjögren); anti-phospholipid (APS, clotting).
- **Pathogenesis**: defective clearance of apoptotic cells → nucleic-acid–containing immune complexes → TLR7/9 + cGAS-STING activation in pDCs → **Type I IFN signature**; immune-complex deposition in glomeruli (lupus nephritis), skin, joints.
- **Therapy**: hydroxychloroquine (foundation); steroids; immunosuppressants (MMF, AZA); **belimumab** (anti-BAFF); **anifrolumab** (anti-IFN-α-receptor); **anti-CD20** (rituximab); now **CAR-T anti-CD19** (Schett 2022 Nature Medicine) showing drug-free remission in severe refractory SLE.

**Multiple sclerosis (MS)** — CNS demyelinating disease.
- Autoreactive T cells (Th1 + Th17) + B cells attack myelin; relapsing-remitting or progressive.
- **CSF**: **oligoclonal bands** (IgG); now MRI-based diagnosis. **HLA-DRB1*15:01** main risk allele.
- **EBV implicated** as essentially-required trigger (Ascherio + Bjornevik 2022 Science — 10M US military serial-serology study showed EBV seroconversion preceded MS; molecular-mimicry with GlialCAM).
- **Therapy**: anti-α4 integrin (natalizumab); S1P modulators (fingolimod, ozanimod); B-cell depletion (**ocrelizumab, ofatumumab** — most effective class); BTK inhibitors (tolebrutinib trials); CAR-T trials emerging.

**Type 1 diabetes (T1D)** — autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β cells.
- Autoantibodies: GAD65, IA-2, ZnT8, insulin.
- Strongest HLA association (DR3-DQ2, DR4-DQ8); polygenic.
- **Teplizumab** (anti-CD3 mAb; FDA 2022) — first disease-modifying therapy; delays diagnosis ~2 yrs in high-risk individuals. Confirms autoimmune nature.
- Closed-loop insulin + islet transplantation + stem-cell-derived β cells (Vertex VX-880 — first clinical trial of stem-cell-derived β cells with transient immunosuppression; 2023+).

**Psoriasis + Crohn's disease + IBD** — Th17 / IL-23 axis.
- **Psoriasis**: IL-23 → Th17 → IL-17 → keratinocyte hyperproliferation + neutrophil infiltrate. **IL-17 blockers** (secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab); **IL-23 blockers** (ustekinumab, risankizumab, guselkumab, tildrakizumab). Among most effective biologics in any disease.
- **Crohn's + UC**: heterogeneous; **TNF** (infliximab, adalimumab), **anti-α4β7** (vedolizumab — gut-selective), **IL-12/23 + IL-23**, **JAK** (tofacitinib UC, upadacitinib both), S1P (ozanimod UC). NOD2 + ATG16L1 + IL23R risk variants.

**Hashimoto's thyroiditis + Graves' disease** — classic organ-specific autoimmunity.
- Hashimoto's: anti-TPO + anti-Tg → hypothyroidism (lymphocytic infiltration).
- Graves': **TSI** (thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin) → hyperthyroidism (auto-agonist mimicking TSH). Teprotumumab (anti-IGF-1R) for thyroid eye disease.
- Sjögren's, primary biliary cholangitis, myasthenia gravis (anti-AChR), pemphigus + pemphigoid (anti-desmoglein, anti-BP180), autoimmune hepatitis, ANCA vasculitis, scleroderma — each defined by characteristic autoantibody + target tissue.

slides.title: Hypersensitivity + allergy + Th2 + Mosmann-Coffman
slides.body:
**Coombs + Gell classification (1963)** — four hypersensitivity types, framework still standard.

**Type I — immediate, IgE-mediated**:
- Allergen + IgE bound to **FcεRI** on mast cells + basophils → cross-linking → degranulation: **histamine**, tryptase, prostaglandins, leukotrienes (LTC4/D4/E4), PAF, cytokines. Late-phase: chemokine-driven eosinophil + Th2 infiltration.
- Manifestations: allergic rhinitis, asthma, atopic dermatitis (eczema), food allergy, anaphylaxis (epinephrine first-line).
- Sensitization in atopic individuals: defective epidermal barrier (filaggrin LOF) + Th2-polarized response to food + environmental allergens.
- Asthma: Th2 + IL-4 + IL-5 + IL-13 → eosinophilia + smooth-muscle hyperreactivity + goblet-cell mucus + airway remodeling. **ILC2s** also major IL-13 source.
- Biologics for severe asthma: **omalizumab** (anti-IgE); **mepolizumab + reslizumab + benralizumab** (anti-IL-5/IL-5R; eosinophilic asthma); **dupilumab** (anti-IL-4Rα; blocks IL-4 + IL-13; transformative in eczema + asthma + EoE + nasal polyposis + COPD); **tezepelumab** (anti-TSLP; upstream alarmin block).
- **Anaphylaxis**: systemic mast-cell degranulation → vasodilation, bronchoconstriction, laryngeal edema, hypotension. Epinephrine reverses; antihistamines + steroids adjunct.

**Type II — antibody-mediated cytotoxicity**:
- IgG/IgM against cell-surface or matrix antigens → opsonization, complement, ADCC.
- Examples: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (warm + cold AIHA), ITP, transfusion reactions (ABO-mismatch), hemolytic disease of the newborn (anti-Rh), **myasthenia gravis** (anti-AChR), Goodpasture's (anti-GBM type IV collagen), pemphigus vulgaris (anti-desmoglein 3).

**Type III — immune complex disease**:
- Soluble antigen + antibody → immune complexes deposit in vessel walls + glomeruli + joints → complement + neutrophil infiltration.
- Examples: serum sickness (post-antitoxin or post-drug), SLE nephritis, Arthus reaction (local), post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis (farmer's lung).

**Type IV — T-cell-mediated, delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH)**:
- 24-72 hr; CD4 Th1 + CD8 + macrophages.
- Examples: **PPD/Mantoux** TB test; contact dermatitis (poison ivy, nickel — haptens modify self-proteins); celiac disease (gluten-reactive CD4 T cells); type 1 diabetes; MS; rheumatoid arthritis; allograft rejection (acute cellular).
- Drug hypersensitivity reactions (SJS/TEN, DRESS) are HLA-restricted T-cell responses to drug-modified peptides (HLA-B*57:01 + abacavir; HLA-B*15:02 + carbamazepine; HLA-B*58:01 + allopurinol).

**Th1 vs Th2 dichotomy — Tim Mosmann + Robert Coffman (1986)** — landmark paper that reorganized cellular immunology by demonstrating T-helper subsets with distinct cytokine programs:
- **Th1**: IFNγ + IL-2 + TNF-β; T-bet master TF; intracellular pathogens + DTH + macrophage activation.
- **Th2**: IL-4 + IL-5 + IL-13 + IL-10; GATA3 master TF; helminths + allergy + B-cell IgE class-switching.
- Mutual cross-regulation: IFNγ inhibits Th2; IL-4 inhibits Th1.
- Extended later by **Th17** (IL-17 + IL-22; RORγt; extracellular bacteria + fungi + autoimmunity), **Tfh** (CXCR5 + IL-21 + BCL-6; B-cell help), **Treg** (FOXP3; suppression), Th9, Th22.
- Mosmann + Coffman's framework remains the conceptual backbone of CD4 biology — directly informing every modern cytokine-targeting biologic (IL-4Rα, IL-5, IL-13, IL-17, IL-23, IL-6, TNF).

**Hygiene + old-friends hypotheses**: Strachan (1989) — reduced childhood infections + larger families = lower allergy risk; refined by Rook + others into the 'old friends' hypothesis emphasizing co-evolution with commensal + helminth exposures (immunoregulatory training of Tregs). Explains the global rise in allergy + autoimmunity in industrialized settings.

question.question: Derive the rationale for using anti-CD20 (rituximab) in autoimmune diseases despite the autoimmune process being thought of as 'T-cell-driven'
question.goal: Reason from B-cell biology + autoantibody pathology + recent CAR-T data why depleting B cells is therapeutically effective across many autoimmune diseases.

steps.prompt: Beyond producing autoantibodies, what other roles do B cells play in autoimmunity?
steps.motivation: B cells are not just antibody factories.

acceptedAnswers: B cells present antigen on MHC-II to T cells, produce inflammatory cytokines, organize ectopic germinal centers in inflamed tissues, + provide signals to T cells

steps.reveal: B cells (1) capture autoantigen via cognate BCR with high affinity → present on MHC-II → activate cognate self-reactive CD4 T cells (a major B-cell role in autoimmunity); (2) produce **cytokines** (IL-6, IL-10, GM-CSF, lymphotoxin); (3) organize ectopic germinal centers + tertiary lymphoid structures in inflamed tissues (synovium in RA, kidney in lupus nephritis, brain meninges in MS); (4) provide costimulation to T cells. Depleting B cells reduces antigen presentation + cytokines + tertiary GC architecture — independent of antibody production.

steps.prompt: Why does anti-CD20 (rituximab) not affect long-lived plasma cells but still works in many autoantibody-driven diseases?

acceptedAnswers: CD20 is on pre-B, naïve, memory B cells but lost on plasma cells; rituximab depletes the precursor pool, drains the GC + memory compartment, + the autoantibody pool decays as plasma cells turn over

hints: CD20 lost on plasmablasts + plasma cells.
steps.reveal: **Plasma cells lack CD20** (downregulated upon differentiation) — rituximab + ocrelizumab + ofatumumab spare LLPCs. The therapeutic effect comes from depleting **memory B cells + germinal-center precursors** (re-fuel of autoreactive plasma cells), eliminating B-cell antigen presentation, + reducing B-cell-derived cytokines. For diseases dominated by short-lived plasmablasts (RA, MS), depletion is sufficient. For LLPC-dominant diseases (myasthenia gravis with steady-state anti-AChR), anti-CD20 may underperform → newer **anti-CD38** (daratumumab — myeloma + AIHA) + **anti-BCMA + CAR-T** target plasma cells directly.

steps.prompt: How does CAR-T anti-CD19 (Schett 2022 SLE data) extend this strategy?

acceptedAnswers: CAR-T anti-CD19 produces deeper + more durable B-cell depletion (including tissue B cells + early plasmablasts) → drug-free remission in severe refractory autoimmune disease

steps.reveal: **Georg Schett (Erlangen) 2022 Nature Medicine + subsequent NEJM 2024** + multiple groups: **anti-CD19 CAR-T** produces deeper, longer, more uniformly tissue-penetrating B-cell depletion than antibodies — including early plasmablasts (CD19⁺ briefly) + tissue B cells. Patients with severe refractory SLE, scleroderma, myositis, MG, MS, RA achieved drug-free remission with B-cell reconstitution from naïve repertoire (apparently 'reset' immunologically — autoantibodies disappeared + did not return upon B-cell reconstitution). Now multiple trials (CABA-201, BMS-986353, autologous + allogeneic CAR-T). Represents potentially curative therapy + a new framework: re-derive a healthy B-cell + plasma-cell compartment from depleted state.

steps.prompt: What does this reveal about the architecture of autoimmunity?

acceptedAnswers: Autoimmunity is sustained by the ongoing supply of self-reactive B + plasma cells from precursor pools; deep depletion + re-derivation can reset the system

steps.reveal: Autoimmunity is a **self-reinforcing steady state** — self-reactive memory B cells + GCs supply continually-renewed autoantibody-producing plasma cells + activate self-reactive T cells. **Deep depletion** + B-cell reconstitution from bone-marrow naïve precursors can **break the steady state** — re-derived B cells appear to be re-tolerized in development. This validates B-cell-centric models of autoimmunity, demonstrates the therapeutic value of complete depletion, + reframes autoimmune disease as potentially curable rather than chronically managed. A genuine paradigm shift built on Burnet's + Rajewsky's + Nussenzweig's B-cell biology.

question.question: Why is the Mosmann-Coffman Th1/Th2 paradigm (1986) considered the conceptual backbone of CD4 T-helper biology?
options: **Tim Mosmann + Robert Coffman (1986)** demonstrated that murine CD4 T-cell clones segregate into **two reproducible cytokine-secretion patterns**: **Th1** (IFNγ + IL-2 + TNF-β) + **Th2** (IL-4 + IL-5 + IL-13 + IL-10), with **mutual cross-regulation** (IFNγ inhibits Th2; IL-4 inhibits Th1). This reorganized cellular immunology: Th1 maps to intracellular-pathogen defense + DTH + macrophage activation + many organ-specific autoimmune diseases; Th2 maps to helminth defense + allergy + IgE class-switching + ILC2-coordinated mucosal repair. Master transcription factors (T-bet → Th1, GATA3 → Th2) consolidated the framework. Extended later by Th17 (IL-17 + IL-22, RORγt; mucosal + autoimmunity), Tfh (CXCR5 + IL-21 + BCL-6; B-cell help), Treg (FOXP3; suppression), Th9, Th22. **Every modern cytokine-targeting biologic** (anti-IL-4Rα dupilumab, anti-IL-5 mepolizumab + benralizumab, anti-IL-13 lebrikizumab, anti-IL-17 secukinumab, anti-IL-23 ustekinumab + risankizumab, anti-IL-6 tocilizumab, anti-TNF) is built on Th-subset biology. Foundational + clinically translated paradigm.
It is only relevant in mice.
question.explanation: Mosmann + Coffman (1986) discovered Th1/Th2 cytokine dichotomy in murine CD4 T-cell clones — Th1 (IFNγ + IL-2) vs Th2 (IL-4 + IL-5 + IL-13) with mutual cross-regulation. Master TFs T-bet + GATA3 consolidated. Extended by Th17 + Tfh + Treg + Th9 + Th22. Foundation of all modern cytokine biologics (dupilumab, mepolizumab, secukinumab, ustekinumab, tocilizumab, anti-TNF). Paradigm-defining + clinically translated.

hints: What did Mosmann + Coffman discover + classify?
slides.workedSolution: Mosmann + Coffman (1986) demonstrated CD4 T-cell clones segregate into Th1 (IFNγ + IL-2) + Th2 (IL-4 + IL-5 + IL-13) with mutual cross-regulation. Th1 → intracellular pathogens + DTH; Th2 → helminths + allergy + IgE. Extended by Th17 + Tfh + Treg + others. Foundation of every modern cytokine biologic.

question.question: Diagnosing + managing complex autoimmunity
question.prompt: A 28-year-old woman presents with malar rash, arthralgias, proteinuria, lymphopenia, low complement, + positive ANA + anti-dsDNA + anti-Sm. (a) What is the most likely diagnosis + which Coombs-Gell hypersensitivity types contribute to which manifestations? (b) Discuss the role of Type I IFN signature, pDCs, TLR7/9 sensing of nucleic-acid immune complexes, + impaired clearance of apoptotic cells. (c) Stage therapy from hydroxychloroquine + steroids to belimumab + anifrolumab + rituximab, + comment on when **CAR-T anti-CD19** (Schett-type) might be considered. (d) How does this case illustrate the failure of central + peripheral tolerance — what genetic + environmental triggers may have contributed?

question.question: Write the simple Bayesian-style expression for the post-test probability (PPV) of an autoimmune disease given a positive autoantibody test result, in terms of sensitivity (Sn), specificity (Sp), + prevalence (P).

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how central + peripheral tolerance fail in autoimmunity + how modern therapy intervenes at multiple immune checkpoints.
question.rubric: Mentions: **Central tolerance**: thymic negative selection + **AIRE** (defective in **APECED**); bone-marrow B-cell deletion + receptor editing. **Peripheral tolerance**: Tregs (**FOXP3**; defective in **IPEX**); anergy; CTLA-4 + PD-1 checkpoints; AICD. Failure causes: HLA risk alleles (HLA-B*27, DR3/DR4, DR15:01); polygenic risk (PTPN22, STAT4, IL-23R); environmental triggers (EBV → MS; smoking → RA; gluten → celiac); molecular mimicry; sex bias. Major diseases: **RA** (anti-CCP, Th17 + TNF + IL-6); **SLE** (anti-dsDNA, Type I IFN, immune complexes); **MS** (Th1 + Th17 + B cells); **T1D** (CD8 destruction of β cells); **psoriasis + IBD** (IL-23/Th17). **Hypersensitivity** (Coombs-Gell I-IV) + **Mosmann-Coffman Th1/Th2** + Th17/Tfh/Treg framework underpins disease classification + biologics. Therapies span anti-TNF, anti-IL-6, anti-IL-17/23, anti-IL-4Rα, anti-CD20 (rituximab/ocrelizumab), anti-α4β7 (vedolizumab), anti-BAFF (belimumab), anti-IFNAR (anifrolumab), CTLA-4-Ig (abatacept), JAK inhibitors, + **CAR-T anti-CD19** (Schett 2022) for refractory SLE — potential reset of autoimmunity.
